title: Notes on the Vessel and the Clock
author: Laboratory Fixture Editor
source_reference: Synthetic research demonstration written for Pretorius-Laboratory; not an imported historical book or character memory.
pages: Page 1. The old laboratory clock gave a dull, measured tick. A vessel stood on the bench, its rim unbroken. The ledger recorded no prior intervention.
Page 2. After twelve experimental ticks, the vessel remained in its original position. Observation and recollection were recorded separately. Neither established an unseen cause.
Page 3. A strip of blue paper marked this page. The next experiment would compare a remembered location with an independently inspected shelf.
